column1: # The fleet's machines: what each one IS, and therefore what may be placed on it.
# name<TAB>ssh<TAB>os/arch<TAB>roles<TAB>seat<TAB>cores<TAB>notes
# roles is a SET from {bench, runner, coordination, services}, comma separated:
#   bench         cards, probes and load may be placed here
#   runner        the machine serves the merge group's CI shards
#   coordination  a friend's own window lives here
#   services      Loki, Grafana, Redis and the rest of the stack live here
# seat is the nova-secrets seat on the machine, or `-` when it carries none.
# notes is free text, or `-`.
# THE LOCK (the coordinator, 2026-09-18): runner hosts are CI-only. No card, no probe and no load may
# be placed on a machine that serves the merge group's shards -- a card and a shard on one
# host make the shard slow, the gate red and the queue stop. `nova-pulse fill` and every
# fleet verb that acts on a machine refuse a name whose roles lack `bench`.
# A machine that is BOTH runner and bench is the exception, not the shape, so it must say so
# in its notes: `allow-shared=<YYYY-MM-DD> <why>`. bench, worker and threadripper-wsl are
# shared today because the pull worker still runs a card in the bench's own home; when it
# runs cards in containers the runner role comes off those lines and this exception goes
# with it.
# THERE IS NO WINDOWS MACHINE IN THIS FILE, and there is not meant to be (the coordinator, 2026-09-18:
# "drop the native windows CI runners. WSL only from now on."). The Threadripper is a
# WINDOWS BOX and it joins the fleet as `threadripper-wsl`, a LINUX machine: WSL2 is the
# operating system the cards and the CI runners see, so `os/arch` is linux/x64, the bench
# standard is the Linux one, and its runners carry the ordinary Linux labels. The native
# half of that box is not a bench and not a runner, so it has no line here.
coordinator
